extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of PARI/GP (mathematicians and script-writers using GP; authors of GP scripts and extensions)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference and usage guidelines for PARI/GP built-in functions, error types, control constructs, and parallel programming interfaces; includes caveats, examples, and library-level interfaces. Intended to guide correct use and script development in GP/PARI.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_ALARM
rubrics_metrics.description: A timeout generated by the alarm function. E has one component (t_STR): the error message to print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised when alarm() times out; examples show alarm returning a t_ERROR and print produces 'error("alarm interrupt after ... ms.")'. Can be trapped via trap/iferr. Also recognized as a trap keyword.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_USER
rubrics_metrics.description: A user error triggered by error(g1,...,gn). E has one component, 1 (t_VEC): the vector of n arguments given to error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by user code calling error(...); appears as t_ERROR when returned by alarm or other contexts. Recognized as a trap keyword.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_CONSTPOL
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument of function s is a constant polynomial, which does not make sense (e.g., galoisinit(Pol(1))). E has one component (t_STR): the function name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates invalid polynomial argument for functions expecting non-constant polynomials; used to provide informative error messages naming the function.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_COPRIME
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s expected coprime arguments, and did receive x, y which were not. E has three components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2: argument x, 3: argument y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised when functions require coprime inputs; error object includes offending arguments for debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_INV
rubrics_metrics.description: Tried to invert a non-invertible object x in function s. E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2: the non-invertible x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x = Mod(a,b) and a is not 0 mod b, e_INV can leak a non-trivial gcd(a,b), enabling factorization. Useful diagnostic when inversion fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_IRREDPOL
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s expected an irreducible polynomial and received T which was not. E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 (t_POL) the polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised by functions requiring irreducibility (e.g., nfinit(x^2-1)). Error object names the function and polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_MISC
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic uncategorized error. E has one component (t_STR): the error message to print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fallback category for miscellaneous errors; appears in trap keyword list.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_MODULUS
rubrics_metrics.description: Moduli x and y submitted to function s are inconsistent. E has three components: 1 (t_STR) function s, 2: argument x, 3: argument y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised when inconsistent modulus data is supplied to functions (example shows mismatch when converting between representations).

rubrics_metrics.name: e_NEGVAL
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument of function s is a power series with negative valuation, which does not make sense. E has one component (t_STR): the function name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., cos(1/x) gives negative valuation error; indicates invalid valuation for operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_PRIME
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s expected a prime number and received p which was not. E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2: the argument p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised by functions that require prime inputs (e.g., idealprimedec(nf, 4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: e_ROOTS0
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument of function s is a zero polynomial, and we need to consider its roots. E has one component (t_STR): the function name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., polroots(0) triggers this condition; not an ordinary input.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_SQRTN
rubrics_metrics.description: Trying to compute an n-th root of x which does not exist, in function s. E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2: the argument x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised when extracting roots fails (e.g., sqrt(Mod(-1,3))).

rubrics_metrics.name: e_ARCH
rubrics_metrics.description: Not available on this architecture or operating system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the trap-recognized error keywords; indicates platform-specific unavailability.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_STACK
rubrics_metrics.description: The PARI stack overflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trap-recognized keyword; indicates stack overflow conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_IMPL
rubrics_metrics.description: Not yet implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised for unimplemented features; appears in trap-recognized keyword list.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_OVERFLOW
rubrics_metrics.description: All forms of arithmetic overflow, including length or exponent overflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trap-recognized keyword indicating arithmetic oversize conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_SYNTAX
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trap-recognized keyword for parsing/syntax errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_TYPE
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trap-recognized keyword when an object has an incorrect type for an operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: next (control statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrupts execution of current seq, resume the next iteration of the innermost enclosing loop (or top-level loop). If n specified, resume at the n-th enclosing loop; if n exceeds number of loops, all enclosing loops are exited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used inside loops to skip to next iteration(s); supports numeric argument to jump multiple nesting levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: return (control statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: return({x = 0}) returns from current subroutine with result x; if x is omitted, returns void (no result).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to return a value from user functions; omission returns nothing like print.

rubrics_metrics.name: until (control statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: until(a, seq) evaluates seq until a is not equal to 0 (i.e., until a is true). The condition is tested after executing seq (do-while semantics). If a is initially true, seq is evaluated once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for do-while style loops; note evaluation semantics differ from while.

rubrics_metrics.name: while (control statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: while(a, seq) evaluates seq while a is non-zero, testing the condition before evaluating seq (standard while). If a is initially zero, seq is never evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard pre-test loop behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strprintf(fmt,{x}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a string built from remaining arguments according to format fmt. Format consists of ordinary characters and conversion specifications (see printf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: String-returning variant of printf formatting; use when you need formatted string values rather than direct output.

rubrics_metrics.name: addhelp(sym,str)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes the help message for symbol sym; str is expanded and stored as online help. Recommended to document global variables and user functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once addhelp is applied to a function, the function code is no longer shown by ?help; original code still accessible by typing the symbol name. You can attach help to aliases but they won't be shown (aliases expand to underlying symbol help). Library prototype: void addhelp(const char *sym,const char *str).

rubrics_metrics.name: alarm({s=0},{code})
rubrics_metrics.description: If code omitted, trigger an e_ALARM exception after s seconds, cancelling previous alarm. If code provided and s positive, evaluate code aborting after s seconds; returns value of code if completed or a t_ERROR otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: alarm(1,factor(N)) returns t_ERROR if timed out. Cannot set a new alarm within another alarm's code (child alarm erases parent). Use to time-bound operations; when timed out returns a t_ERROR object which can be tested and replaced by fallback computations (example timefact).

rubrics_metrics.name: alias(newsym,sym)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines newsym as an alias for sym. Alias expansion is performed at compilation time and affects only GP code compiled after alias is evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can alias member functions and operators using internal names; aliasing does not affect previously compiled/defined functions (see example showing prior definitions unaffected). To create run-time flexible behavior use variables instead. Library syntax: void alias0(const char *newsym,const char *sym).

rubrics_metrics.name: allocatemem({s=0}) usage and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes the stack size after initialization. If x>0, allocates new stack of at least x bytes (may allocate more). If x=0, new stack size = twice old. The old stack is discarded and function ends with a longjmp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be typed at gp prompt in interactive use or left by itself at start of batch files. Cannot be used inside loop-like constructs or as part of larger expression sequences (e.g., 'allocatemem(); x=1;' will not set x). All pending sequences are discarded due to stack move and longjmp. If OS cannot allocate requested size, allocation is halved in a loop until success, with warnings printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: apply(f,A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply closure f to entries of A. If A scalar returns f(A). If polynomial or power series applies to coefficients. For vector or list returns f(x) for each element. For matrix returns matrix of f(A[i,j]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many functions act componentwise on vectors/matrices but not lists, so apply is useful for lists. Shortcuts: set-notation comprehensions [g(x)|x<-v,f(x)] etc. Example: apply on list of modulars then lift to integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: default({key},{val})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the default corresponding to keyword key. If val present, sets the default to val first (subject to string expansion). default() lists all defaults and values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortcuts exist for interactive use; see sections referenced for list of defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: errname(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the type of the error message E as a string (i.e., error name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to inspect t_ERROR objects created by alarm or error.

rubrics_metrics.name: error({str}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs its argument list (each interpreted as a string), then interrupts the running GP program, returning to prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to raise user errors with custom messages (e.g., error('n = ', n, ' is not squarefree!')).

rubrics_metrics.name: extern(str) and externstr(str)
rubrics_metrics.description: extern(str) runs external shell command str immediately and feeds its output into gp as if read from a file. externstr(str) runs command and returns its output as a vector of GP strings (one per output line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to integrate shell commands; extern writes into gp input while externstr returns strings for programmatic use.

rubrics_metrics.name: getabstime(), gettime(), getstack(), getheap(), getrand(), getenv()
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility functions: getabstime returns ms since gp startup (reentrant); gettime returns ms since last gettime or current instruction; getstack returns bytes used on stack; getheap returns number of objects and memory they occupy; getrand returns current PRNG seed internal state; getenv returns environment variable value or 0 if undefined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for timing, debugging, reproducibility (getrand/setrand), and environment interrogation.

rubrics_metrics.name: global(listof variables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Marked obsolete and scheduled for deletion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use new code; maintainers plan to remove function.

rubrics_metrics.name: inline(x,...,z) and uninline()
rubrics_metrics.description: inline declares variables as inline with unlimited scope, behaving like lexically scoped my() but global; uninline exits scope of inline variables. Recommended to call uninline() before script end to avoid leaking inline variables outside the script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental feature; use uninline() to avoid leaking. Inline variables can be exited using uninline().

rubrics_metrics.name: input()
rubrics_metrics.description: Reads a string interpreted as a GP expression from input file (usually keyboard); if sequence of expressions given returns result of last expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using gp under Emacs (pari.el) you must prompt for the string with same prompt as previous ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: install(name,code,{gpname},{lib}) and prototype rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Loads from dynamic library lib the function name and assigns it to gpname in session with prototype code. Gives access to non-static functions in PARI library and allows adding external functions to gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prototype encoding: first char i/l/v for return type, one-letter codes for mandatory arg types (G,&,L,s,n), p/P for precisions, DG/D&/Dn for optional args, etc. Caution: may segfault on statically linked gp on first use; test with harmless example before relying on it. Re-installing updates prototype but does not reload symbol from library.

rubrics_metrics.name: kill(sym)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restores symbol sym to 'undefined' status and deletes any help messages associated with sym (added by addhelp). Variable names remain known to interpreter and keep their former priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Killing a user function does not remove its name from variable list. To reset variables to starting values without deleting help use quoting (a='a). Only kill can remove aliases and installed functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: print and print1
rubrics_metrics.description: print({str}*) outputs string arguments in raw format ending with newline. print1 outputs without trailing newline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use print1 for prompts; can embed newlines inside strings with \n.

rubrics_metrics.name: printf(fmt,{x}*) formatting semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Prints arguments according to fmt, supporting ordinary characters and conversion specifications with flags (#,0,-,+,space), field width (digits or *), precision (.digits or *), and conversion specifiers (d,i,o,u,x,X,p,e,E,f,F,g,G,c,s,%). Length modifier is ignored in gp except l and P are described for libpari.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of each flag and conversion's effect are given. Notable deviations from C89/C99: when precision missing uses current realprecision; exponent formatting differences; switching to e style in some f cases; g/G do not strip trailing zeros or trailing decimal point; 0 printed as 0.Eexp. Examples show use of flags, field width and precision passed by argument, recursive application to vectors/matrices, and common formatting idioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: printf technical deviations (GP-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: GP's printf deviates from C standards: missing precision uses current realprecision; e conversion does not enforce two-digit exponent or + sign in exponent; f may switch to e when exponent >= precision; g/G keep trailing zeros and decimal point; 0 printed as 0.Eexp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of these differences when porting code or expecting C-like formatting; examples show resulting outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: printsep and printsep1
rubrics_metrics.description: printsep(sep,{str}*) prints arguments separated by sep and ends with newline. printsep1 does same without trailing newline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for custom-separated output; examples show printing with ':' separator.

rubrics_metrics.name: printtex and writetex
rubrics_metrics.description: printtex({str}*) outputs strings in TeX format to standard output. writetex(filename,{str}*) writes (appends) the strings to filename in TeX format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable log default or set logfile to capture TeX output for manuscripts; use writetex to write to files.

rubrics_metrics.name: quit({status=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Exits gp and returns to system with exit status (small integer). System actually sees status mod 256.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-zero status normally indicates abnormal termination. See system man pages for exit(3)/wait(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: read({filename}), readstr({filename}), readvec({filename})
rubrics_metrics.description: read reads and evaluates file filename (subject to string expansion); returns result of last expression. readstr returns vector of GP strings (one per line). readvec returns a vector of evaluation results of all sequences in file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If file contains allocatemem, leave read instructions by themselves as allocatemem causes longjmp and discards pending sequences. Binary GP files can be read and will return last object. readvec useful to import many separate results. Underlying library functions provided for C API.

rubrics_metrics.name: select(f,A,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vector or list A and closure f, select returns elements x of A such that f(x) is non-zero (boolean selection). If A is a matrix, selects columns and returns matrix of selected columns. If flag=1 returns indices of selected elements (indirect selection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set-notation shortcuts available ([g(x)|x<-v,f(x)] etc.). To remove entries use select with negated predicate. Example shows selecting primes from vector(i^2+1). Use vecextract with index result to recover elements from indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: setrand(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reseeds the random number generator using seed n. No value returned. Seed can be technical array from getrand or a small positive integer to deterministically generate state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use setrand to make randomized computations reproducible. Example: starting with setrand(1) twice will reproduce exact same output sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: system(str)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executes system command str, outputs result to standard output (not into logfile), and returns control to PARI system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple wrapper around C system(); output goes to terminal not log.

rubrics_metrics.name: trap({e},{rec},seq) (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete function: tries to evaluate seq trapping runtime error e; if error occurs runs recovery sequence rec and returns that as result. If e omitted, traps all exceptions. Use iferr instead (recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior: seq evaluated up to point producing error; recovery evaluated from same context (does not undo prior side-effects). Example provided to trap division by zero. Current recognized keywords listed (see errors above). Library syntax GEN trap0(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: type(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the internal type name of PARI object x as a string (e.g., "t_INT").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful under gp for debugging; macro typ returns a long matching t_* symbols and may be simpler for branching.

rubrics_metrics.name: version()
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns current version number as t_VEC with three integer components (major, minor, patchlevel); development checkouts may append further components (commit count, git hash).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: lex() can compare version vectors for conditional code. For released versions first three numeric components suffice. Example shows formatting of GP/PARI version string using printf and including optional components for development builds.

rubrics_metrics.name: warning({str}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs the message 'user warning' and the argument list (each interpreted as a string); if colors enabled, warning displayed in different color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to indicate non-fatal issues; example: warning(n, ' is very large, this might take a while.').

rubrics_metrics.name: whatnow(key)
rubrics_metrics.description: If key is name of a function that was present in GP version 1.39.15 or lower, outputs the new function name and syntax if it changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps migrate old scripts to newer GP versions when functions have been renamed or syntax changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: write(filename,{str}*) and write1
rubrics_metrics.description: write appends arguments (as strings) to filename and appends a newline (same output as print). write1 does same without trailing newline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to save textual outputs. For exact internal structures use writebin (binary).

rubrics_metrics.name: writebin(filename,{x}) and binary file caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Writes (appends) object x in binary format to filename. Format stores exact internal structure and is faster to save/load than text expressions. If x omitted, saves all user variables with names. Binary files include magic number so read recognizes them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installed functions and history objects cannot be saved. If saved objects refer to polynomial variables not defined in new session they'll display oddly. Binary files can be gzipped. Important caveat: binary files are architecture-dependent and future compatibility not guaranteed, so do not use for long-term storage; they are larger and harder to compress than text.

rubrics_metrics.name: parapply(f,x) (parallel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel evaluation of f on elements of x. Closure f must not access global variables or variables declared with local(), and must be free of side-effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires PARI configured with multithreading; works with POSIX threads or MPI. Properly written GP program should work identically with either backend. Example shows factoring large numbers in parallel and computing elliptic curve orders in parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: pareval(x) (parallel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel evaluation of elements of x where x is a vector of closures. Closures must be arity 0, must not access global/local variables and must be side-effect free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to evaluate multiple independent zero-argument closures concurrently.

rubrics_metrics.name: parfor(i = a,{b},expr1,{j},{expr2}) and execution semantics (parallel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates expr2 (dependent on i and j) for i between a and b in random order, computed in parallel. Substitute j by expr1(i). If b omitted loop will not stop. expr2 may use break/next/return but even then expr2 will still be evaluated for all remaining values of i less than current one unless a subsequent break/next/return happens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parfor semantics are non-deterministic in order; control-flow interruptions do not prevent some remaining iterations from running (careful when using break/next/return).

rubrics_metrics.name: parforprime(p = a,{b},expr1,{j},{expr2})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like parfor but iterates over primes p between a and b in random order, computed in parallel. Substitute j by expr1(p). Same semantics for break/next/return as parfor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenient for prime-indexed parallel computations; be cautious about non-deterministic order and partial termination semantics.
